2022_262_mhsaa_5_1_22_rcminutes_web.paragraph: Minutes of the Michigan High School Athletic Association Representative Council meeting held in East Lansing on May 1-2, 2022, distributed to member boards of education with a note that changes take effect Aug. 1, 2022 unless otherwise indicated. The Council received membership, eligibility, officials and legislative reports and adopted regulation changes covering transfers, amateur status, out-of-state contests and violation penalties, plus sport-specific rules in baseball, bowling, competitive cheer, football, golf, ice hockey, soccer, swimming and diving, tennis and wrestling. It approved the 2022-23 budget on a motion by Chris Miller supported by Jason Mensing, built on revenue projections of just over $12,000,000 and expense projections of $11,500,000.
2022_262_mhsaa_5_1_22_rcminutes_web.page:
**Meeting**
Michigan High School Athletic Association, Inc., Representative Council meeting, East Lansing, May 1-2, 2022. Mark Uyl served as recorder. Kyle Guerrant of Lansing was the only member recorded absent. Council members present included Eric Albright (Midland), Jay Alexander (Detroit), Brad Bush (Chelsea), Nicole Carter (Novi), Judy Cox (Auburn), Scott Grimes (Grand Haven), Kris Isom (Adrian), Sean Jacques (Calumet), Jason Malloy (Westland), Mark Mattson (Maple City), Jason Mensing (Ottawa Lake), Vic Michaels (Detroit), Chris Miller (Gobles), Chris Riker (Portage), Meg Seng (Ann Arbor), Adam Stefanski (Boyne City), John Thompson (Brighton) and Alex Tiseo (Marquette). A motion by Chris Miller, supported by Chris Riker, approved minutes of the March 25, 2022 Council meeting, the March 24 and April 20, 2022 Executive Committee meetings, and the April 21, 2022 Upper Peninsula Athletic Committee meeting.

**Membership and Participation Data**

| Item | Figure |
|---|---|
| High school members (April 1, 2022) | 750 |
| Junior high/middle school members (April 1, 2022) | 759 |
| High schools / JH-MS (April 1, 2021) | 747 / 751 |
| Elementary schools with 6th-grade participation | 62 |
| HS cooperative agreements / teams (April 4, 2022) | 378 / 699 |
| JH-MS cooperative agreements / teams | 90 / 343 |
| Eligibility advancement applications, 2021-22 | none |
| Educational Transfer Forms, 2021-22 through April 5, 2022 | 142 |
| Out-of-State Practice travel forms, 2021-22 | 45 |

Public-to-public transfers remained most common (80); the boarding school exception (#13) became the most frequent reason (56), moving the divorce exception (#8) to second (54). Athletic Director In-Service and Update programs attracted more than 859 registrants in 2021-22. The Coaches Advancement Program involved more than 2,000 participants in 2021-22 with over 1,300 registrations in CAP 1, and more than 33,000 CAP levels completed since the start of 2004-05.

**Reports**
Officials' registrations continued a decade-long decline, described as a near-crisis, with lack of sportsmanship from adults, coaches and spectators cited as a reason officials leave. Staff reported on the NFHS Experience project and national issues including transgender policy, NIL and amateurism. Legislative report noted athletic team and gender identification language in the Michigan House budget bill but not in Senate or Governor's proposals, monitored by Governmental Consultant Services, Inc. Litigation: MHSAA is not involved in public, legislative or judicial challenges; an update was given on UP soccer.

**Ongoing Business**
Football playoff format discussion covered Strength of Schedule qualification plus two alternates, with three approaches to go out on the fall 2022 school tour and a Football Committee meeting before December 2022. A sportsmanship initiative using officials' ratings moves to the Officials Review Committee. An awards task force will report in December of 2022. The redesigned MHSAA website was scheduled to launch by Aug. 1, 2022.

**Selected Adopted Actions**
Interpretation 65 clarified that "parent/parents" includes stepparents and defined the family unit. Interpretation 150 barred paid or compensated endorsements and posing in school uniform for commercial enterprises. Minnesota was added to all border-state references. Regulation V, Section 4(D) penalties were expanded. Junior high/middle school wrestling added 215 lb. and 245 lb. classes, with heavyweights at least 246 lbs. and not over 285 lbs. Bowling Regionals move to eight Baker games and two regular games. Golf's maximum strokes per hole dropped from 12 to 10. A $75 tennis ball and facility fee was adopted for Regional and Final tournaments. Meeting expenses were approved at the specified hotel rate, IRS-stipulated meal amounts and a 40 cents per mile round-trip allowance.

**Budget**
A 2021-22 budget surplus of $877,564 was reported, attributed almost entirely to Payroll Protection Program and Employee Retention credits plus investment conditions. The $500,000 PNC Bank line of credit drawn beginning in early summer of 2020 was fully repaid in December of 2020. The 2022-23 budget carries no ticket price increases, $200,000 for the website redesign (was $100,000 in 2021-22), roughly $200,000 more for officiating including NASO membership, revenue projections of just over $12,000,000 (was $12,244,800 in 2021-22) and expense projections of $11,500,000 (was $11,234,805 in 2021-22).
2022_262_mhsaa_5_1_22_rcminutes_web.verbose:
Minutes of the Michigan High School Athletic Association, Inc. Representative Council meeting held in East Lansing on May 1-2, 2022, with a cover note asking recipients to copy and share with their Board of Education and staff and stating that unless otherwise indicated, changes made by the Representative Council take effect on Aug. 1, 2022.

ATTENDANCE. Members present: Eric Albright, Midland; Jay Alexander, Detroit; Brad Bush, Chelsea; Nicole Carter, Novi; Judy Cox, Auburn; Scott Grimes, Grand Haven; Kris Isom, Adrian; Sean Jacques, Calumet; Jason Malloy, Westland; Mark Mattson, Maple City; Jason Mensing, Ottawa Lake; Vic Michaels, Detroit; Chris Miller, Gobles; Chris Riker, Portage; Meg Seng, Ann Arbor; Adam Stefanski, Boyne City; John Thompson, Brighton; and Alex Tiseo, Marquette. Member absent: Kyle Guerrant, Lansing. Staff members present: Tony Bihn, Sam Davis, Andy Frushour, Dan Hutcheson, Cody Inglis, Karen Jackson, Geoff Kimmerly, Cole Malatinsky, Will McKoy, Andi Osters, Brent Rice, Jon Ross, Mark Uyl (Recorder), Kathy Westdorp and Paige Winne.

ACCOUNTS OF MEETINGS. Motion by Chris Miller, supported by Chris Riker, to approve the minutes of the Representative Council meeting of March 25, 2022; the Executive Committee meeting minutes of March 24 and April 20, 2022; and the Upper Peninsula Athletic Committee meeting minutes of April 21, 2022. Adopted.

ADMINISTRATION REPORT. MHSAA membership during the 2021-22 school year was 750 high schools and 759 junior high/middle schools as of April 1, 2022, compared with 747 and 751 respectively as of April 1, 2021. There were 62 elementary schools with 6th-grader participation. As of April 4, 2022 there were 378 cooperative program agreements for high schools covering 699 teams, an increase of 13 programs and 59 teams over the previous year, and 90 cooperative program agreements covering 343 teams at the junior high/middle school level, an increase of 4 programs and 13 teams. The most frequent high school cooperative sports, in order, are ice hockey, girls and boys swimming and diving, boys lacrosse and girls softball; at the junior high/middle school level they are boys and girls track and field, football, and boys and girls cross country.

Eligibility advancement applications: none were received during 2021-22, the lowest number since the provision began during the 1987-88 school year. Prior-year counts cited: 0 during 2020-21, 3 during 2019-20, 3 during 2018-19, 6 during 2017-18, 5 during 2016-17, 5 during 2015-16, 4 during 2014-15, 14 during 2013-14, 15 during 2012-13, 9 during 2011-12, 15 during 2010-11, 2009-10 and 2008-09, and 7 during 2007-08. The highest number of applications was 94 during the 1991-92 school year.

Educational Transfer Forms: 142 were processed for 2021-22 through April 5, 2022. Other than 110 during 2020-21 (noted as not comparable because of the COVID-19 pandemic), previous years were 213 for 2019-20, 215 for 2018-19, 219 for 2017-18, 237 for 2016-17 and 266 for 2015-16. Public-to-public school transfers continue to be the most common (80), and the boarding school exception (#13) for the first time is the most frequent reason (56), pushing the divorce exception (#8) to second (54).

Travel Forms for Out-of-State Practice: 45 were filed during 2021-22, compared to 6 the year before during the pandemic. The highest number filed was 113 during 2007-08 and the lowest was 40 during 2003-04; the requirement began in 1994-95. Staff will monitor these numbers in light of the recent change allowing teams on spring break to hold up to four scrimmages against other MHSAA member school teams.

A listing of violations by schools and officials between April 9, 2021 and April 8, 2022 indicated the total number of violations for the year was much higher for officials than in any previous year since 2008-09, while school violations were close to pre-pandemic numbers; staff reported an increase in undue influence violations and significant penalties for schools and coaches.

Athletic Director In-Service and Update Meeting programs attracted more than 859 registrants in 2021-22; the fall 2022 in-person schedule was presented and topics identified during the meeting. For the 12th year, two in-service programs for athletic department administrative assistants are planned for September. The Coaches Advancement Program (CAP) involved more than 2,000 participants in 2021-22, with over 1,300 registrations in CAP 1; by year end individuals will have completed more than 33,000 CAP levels since the start of the 2004-05 school year, with added-value benefits of insurance, GamePlans and SCECHs.

The decade-long decline in officials' registrations continued through 2021-22, with extensive discussion of this near-crisis situation and expanded financial resources for recruitment and retention strategies; lack of sportsmanship from adults, coaches and spectators was cited as a reason officials leave. Officials Reports for spring 2021, fall 2021 and winter 2021-22 were provided, broken down by sport and by level (varsity, junior varsity, and sometimes 9th-, 8th- and 7th-grade). Repeat offenders among ejected coaches and players, who must complete an online sportsmanship course before returning, were extremely low.

NATIONAL FEDERATION. Staff updated the Council on the "NFHS Experience" project involving acquisition and partnership with best-in-class technology partners, and on national issues including transgender policy, NIL, amateurism and NCAA challenges. An NFHS Network update covered current schools, number of events and future plans; significant changes to MHSAA multimedia regulations on live regular season video streaming were made at the December 2021 Council meeting for schools that are part of the NFHS Network.

LEGISLATION AND LITIGATION. The current focus in the State Legislature is the budget process; language regarding athletic teams and gender identification was included in the Michigan House budget bill but absent from both the Senate and Governor's office proposals, with Governmental Consultant Services, Inc. continuing to monitor. The MHSAA is not involved in public, legislative or judicial challenges; an update was provided on recent legal activity involving UP soccer.

ONGOING BUSINESS. Results of a Representative Council and staff prioritization poll were shared to help chart areas of focus for 2022-23 and beyond. On football playoffs, the Council discussed the current Strength of Schedule qualification format plus two alternate approaches, one including almost all schools in the tournament and one establishing regular season scheduling groups or pods; three approaches will go out for school review and input during the fall 2022 tour, and the Football Committee will meet prior to December of 2022. A sportsmanship initiative using officials' ratings connected to their assignments as feedback for schools moves to the Officials Review Committee, with possible rating categories and awards for top-placing schools. On MHSAA Awards, hurdles include lack of knowledge of what each award honors and concerns on deadlines, timelines and candidate pools; a small task force will return a recommendation to the Council in December of 2022. Staff shared a website design update scheduled to launch by Aug. 1, 2022.

REGULATIONS. Regulations I through V of the MHSAA Handbook and their interpretations were submitted for review. Motion by Kris Isom, supported by Jason Malloy, to approve the consent package of miscellaneous changes for organization, clarity or updating. Adopted. Regulation I, Section 9, Interpretation 65 - motion by Sean Jacques, supported by Chris Miller: references to "parent/parents" include stepparents; references to "persons with whom the student was/has been living" (the family unit) always include parents whether married or not and minor siblings, and depending on circumstances may include adult siblings, stepsiblings, aunts, uncles, grandparents and significant others living in the dwelling for at least 12 months as part of the family unit and not merely financially self-sufficient co-inhabitants. Adopted. Regulation I, Section 11, Interpretation 150 - motion by Jason Malloy, supported by Mark Mattson: a student may never be paid or given merchandise or privileges for a commercial endorsement, autograph, photograph or appearance fee based on athletic participation, ability, achievements or potential in MHSAA tournament sports, and may not pose in the school's athletic uniform to promote a for-profit or non-profit non-school commercial enterprise even if unpaid. Adopted. Regulation II, Section 6(B) - motion by Sean Jacques, supported by Chris Riker, to add Minnesota to all border state references. Adopted. Regulation II, Section 11(H) 2 a (5) - motion by Vic Michaels, supported by John Thompson, to not adopt a new provision that would have barred school coaches from coaching more than four students in grades 7-12 outside the school season during the school year (Monday the week of Aug. 15 through the Sunday after Memorial Day) while permitting up to six designated contact dates (eight in ice hockey) in windows of Sept. 6-Oct. 16, Dec. 12-Feb. 26 and April 17-June 4. Adopted (no change). Regulation V, Section 4(D) - motion by Adam Stefanski, supported by Jay Alexander: competing in violation of the limitations of Regulation II or IV forfeits the entire meet or contest; students or teams exceeding season limitations under Regulation II, Section 11(A) may not participate in that season's MHSAA tournament in that sport; contests in excess of the season maximum are forfeited; teams violating the fifth quarter regulation forfeit the contest in which the violation occurred, and head coaches in violation are ineligible for the next day of competition. Adopted.

CLASSIFICATION AND JUNIOR HIGH/MIDDLE SCHOOLS. The Summary of MHSAA Tournament Classification for 2022-23 was provided. Motion by Jason Mensing, supported by Brad Bush, to add 215 lb. and 245 lb. junior high/middle school wrestling weight classes, with all HWT contestants weighing at least 246 lbs. and the maximum not exceeding 285 lbs. Adopted. Motion by Kris Isom, supported by Chris Miller, on time between wrestling matches: 1st period 1 1/2 min., 2nd period 1 min., 3rd period 1 min., allowing time between an individual's matches to be reduced from 45 minutes to 35 minutes. Adopted. Motion by Chris Miller, supported by Nicole Carter, to conduct Regional Junior High/Middle School Track and Field Meets beginning in the spring of 2022-23. Adopted. Motion by Eric Albright, supported by Chris Miller, to allow leagues, conferences or independent member schools to request use of the fifth-quarter rule with roster size data, rationale and support of league members or opponents. Adopted.

OFFICIALS. Motion by Jason Mensing, supported by Jay Alexander, to permit Smitty "bright blue" uniforms with horizontal MHSAA logo for volleyball and swim officials beginning in 2023-24 provided all officials present wear the same color, with white remaining the default. Adopted. Motion by Vic Michaels, supported by Sean Jacques, to permit video review by MHSAA staff of ejections in cases of clear misidentification, rules misapplication, or incontrovertible video evidence of error in an ejection or suspension for flagrant contact. Adopted. Motion by Vic Michaels, supported by Jason Mensing, to reduce to five the number of days in which a contract may be cancelled under the Non-Act of God Cancellation Policy without payment due to scheduled officials. Adopted.

SPORTS ACTIVITIES. Baseball: motion by Kris Isom, supported by Brad Bush, to separate the Baseball/Softball Site Selection Committee into individual committees. Adopted. Bowling: motion by Jason Malloy, supported by Adam Stefanski, limiting participants to five balls in the bowling center and two in the bowlers area, adopted; motion by Kris Isom, supported by Eric Albright, to not approve a six-participant Regional and Final roster, adopted (no change); motion by Chris Miller, supported by Jason Mensing, to turn off foul lights during MHSAA tournaments with an honor system, first foul a warning and subsequent fouls a zero for that frame, adopted; motion by Jason Mensing, supported by Vic Michaels, changing the Regional team format to eight Baker games and two regular games, from six Baker games and three regular games, adopted. Girls Competitive Cheer: motion by Brad Bush, supported by Vic Michaels, to not remove the 10-point penalty for fewer than the division-mandated number in Round 2, adopted (no change); motion by Kris Isom, supported by Brad Bush, setting one penalty point per second over the time limit not to exceed 15 points, adopted; motion by John Thompson, supported by Chris Miller, adopting a new choreography chart awarding points for tumbling, OLEs, vertical twists/360s and release skills, not superseding a 10-point maximum, no earlier than 2023-24, adopted; motion by Vic Michaels, supported by John Thompson, to not permit participation on two teams the same date in the same sport with a four-round limit, adopted (no change); motion by Kris Isom, supported by Jason Malloy, allowing middle school teams to perform an OLE in a pyramid with one bracer, liberty flair only, two points of contact, adopted. Football: motion by Brad Bush, supported by Mark Mattson, expanding instant replay for the 11-player Finals to allow head coaches one challenge, adopted; motions to exempt special teams plays from the five-quarter rule and to amend the ejection regulation to four full quarters were not approved (no change); motion by John Thompson, supported by Jason Malloy, allowing shoulder pads at college camps sponsored and run directly by NCAA/NAIA institutions, adopted; the recommendation to seed playoff Regionals instead of Districts was tabled. Golf: motion by John Thompson, supported by Jay Alexander, allowing two school-approved coaches to be present and actively coaching during MHSAA Tournament competition and reducing maximum strokes per hole from 12 to 10, adopted. Ice Hockey: motion by Kris Isom, supported by Eric Albright, to use Michigan Power Ratings to seed the entire Regional round, adopted; motion by Chris Riker, supported by Jason Mensing, to reseed after Quarterfinals with the top-ranked team playing the fourth seed and the second seed playing the third in each of the three divisions, seeds set by a seeding committee on Sunday after Quarterfinal play, adopted; motion by Vic Michaels, supported by Kris Isom, to realign divisions by placing one-third of stand-alone and one-third of cooperative hockey programs in each of the three divisions, adopted. Boys Lacrosse: two committee recommendations on fifth quarters were tabled until the committee meets in October 2022. Soccer: motion by Jason Mensing, supported by Mark Mattson, allowing no more than three halves on a day not followed by a school day, adopted; motion by Kris Isom, supported by Eric Albright, giving the two seeded teams hosting opportunity for games not at a prearranged District host site, with #1 seed priority then #2 seed then the top bracket line, adopted. Swimming and Diving: motion by John Thompson, supported by Kris Isom, giving each Diving Regional ten guaranteed qualifiers to the Final meet with the remaining six spots distributed to Regionals having one of the top six returning divers, adopted. Tennis: motion by Chris Miller, supported by Brad Bush, permitting up to seven seeds with 21 to 23 #1 singles players in the draw and up to eight with 24 or more, adopted; motion by Kris Isom, supported by Nicole Carter, charging all tennis schools a tennis ball and facility fee of $75 for Regional and Final tournaments, similar to golf greens fees and bowling line fees, adopted. Wrestling: motion by Chris Riker, supported by Jason Malloy, approving the new 14 boys and 14 girls NFHS weight classes effective for 2022-23. Adopted.

OPERATIONS. Motion by Jason Mensing, supported by Jay Alexander, approving the Quick Reference Calendars for 2022-23 and 2023-24 and the seven-year calendar of MHSAA events. Adopted; it was noted that in 2023-24 and 2024-25 the Boys and Girls Basketball Tournament dates will switch, with boys playing before girls. For the Allen W. Bush Award, Council members were invited to vote for up to two candidates from the four presented, with winners notified in May, honored during fall of 2022 or early 2023, and featured in the fall issue of benchmarks. Motion by Sean Jacques, supported by Nicole Carter, approving meeting expenses at the specified hotel rate, IRS-stipulated amounts for meals, and a 40 cents per mile mileage allowance, round trip. Adopted. Future meetings: the next Representative Council meeting is Dec. 2, 2022 at the Jack Roberts Building in East Lansing; the March meeting is the morning of Friday, March 24, 2022 as printed; the May meeting will be Sunday and Monday, May 7 and 8, 2023.

BUDGET. Reviewing finances since COVID hit in March of 2020, staff reported the association managed severe reductions in tournament revenue, with notable accomplishments including a budget surplus of $877,564 in 2021-22 attributed almost entirely to federal assistance through the Payroll Protection Program and Employee Retention credits along with good stock market conditions in the investment portfolio. The MHSAA fully repaid the $500,000 line-of-credit from PNC Bank that was needed beginning in early summer of 2020; solid fall tournament numbers allowed it to be paid in December of 2020. A profitable fiscal year 2021-22 was anticipated with spring tournaments determining the size of the surplus. The 2022-23 budget includes no ticket price increases, continued GoFan digital ticketing, and capital improvements delayed until 2023-24 including roof work. It includes $200,000 for completion of the website redesign (was $100,000 in 2021-22) and an additional investment in officiating of approximately $200,000 with National Association of Sports Officials (NASO) membership for all registered officials and an increase in tournament game fees. No new staff were recommended for 2022-23, based on the past four months of internal reorganization. Revenue projections were just over $12,000,000 (was $12,244,800 in 2021-22) and expense projections $11,500,000 (was $11,234,805 in 2021-22), with the expense increase attributed to reorganization of GoFan ticket fees and the officiating investment. Motion by Chris Miller, supported by Jason Mensing, to approve the 2022-23 budget. Adopted.

2022_263_mhsaa_athletes_accident_medical.paragraph: Michigan High School Athletic Association summary of the Athletes and Officials Accident Medical Insurance and Concussion Care Insurance programs provided to member high schools and junior high/middle schools for 2022-23. The accident medical policy, in place since the 1970-71 school year and paid for by the MHSAA at no cost to eligible athletes and registered officials, pays up to $1,000,000 in medical expenses after a $25,000 per-claim deductible in paid medical expenses is met. The separate concussion program, in place since 2015-16, carries a policy limit of $25,000 for each accident.
2022_263_mhsaa_athletes_accident_medical.page:
**Program Overview**
The Michigan High School Athletic Association has provided participants at each member school and all registered officials with excess accident medical insurance since the 1970-71 school year. The notice states it is not intended to be a complete description of coverage and exclusions.

**Who and What Is Covered**
Coverage applies to grades 6-12 for students accidentally injured while engaged in interscholastic athletic activities under MHSAA jurisdiction, namely baseball, basketball (boys and girls), bowling (boys and girls), cross country (boys and girls), football, golf (boys and girls), gymnastics (girls), competitive cheer (girls), ice hockey, lacrosse (boys and girls), soccer (boys and girls), softball (girls), alpine skiing (boys and girls), swimming and diving (boys and girls), tennis (boys and girls), track and field (boys and girls), volleyball (girls), and wrestling. Students are covered when their principal attests in writing and the MHSAA agrees they were eligible under all MHSAA regulations at the time of injury; while traveling directly to and from a scheduled event in school-sponsored transportation as a representative of the school; and while participating in season in an allowed activity under the direct supervision of a full-time school employee or designated coach in sports for which the MHSAA provides a tournament series.

Student-athletes ineligible under MHSAA Regulations are not covered. Students ineligible only under local school rules are covered if allowed to practice with the team, as are students suspended from contests under Regulation V, Section 3 who continue practicing. Officials must be on the premises of the contest worked. Sideline cheerleaders are covered traveling to and from events in school-sponsored transportation and while cheering under direct supervision of a designated school employee, provided their activity does not exceed the safety norms of MHSAA Girls Competitive Cheer for height of mounts, flips and stunts. The coverage does not apply to any out-of-season activities or activities beyond the mileage limits of Regulation II, Section 6, Interpretation 193, even if not expressly prohibited.

**Accident Medical Benefits**

| Benefit | Amount |
|---|---|
| Medical expense maximum | $1,000,000 |
| Deductible in paid medical expenses per claim | $25,000 |
| Paralysis or coma cash benefit | up to $50,000 |
| Accidental death or dismemberment | $10,000 |

The MHSAA is the policyholder and pays the premium; the program pays expenses above the $25,000 deductible left unpaid by parents' or officials' insurance or other sources such as school-purchased insurance. The paralysis or coma condition must occur within 180 days after the accident, and payment is withheld until a physician certifies after a 16-month waiting period that the injury is permanent and irreversible. The first medical expense must be incurred within 90 days after the accident date, and the accidental death or dismemberment benefit applies if either event occurs within 365 days.

**Concussion Care Insurance**
Provided since the 2015-16 school year to athletic participants at each MHSAA member junior high/middle school and high school, paying accident medical expense benefits resulting from concussion sustained during an MHSAA in-season covered activity (in-season practice or competition). Policy limit is $25,000 for each accident. Covered students, sports and situations follow the accident medical insurance. The program is intended to assure that eligible student-athletes in grades 6 through 12, male and female, in all levels of all sports under MHSAA jurisdiction receive prompt professional attention for head injury events even if uninsured or under-insured; deductibles and co-pays left unpaid by other policies are reimbursed.

**Claims Administrators**
Accident medical: Mr. Bryan Cronen, FIRST AGENCY, INC., 5071 West H Avenue, Kalamazoo, MI 49009-8501; Phone 269.381.6630; Fax 269.381.3055; Email Bryan Cronen@aig.com. Concussion care: Cheryl Walsh, Mutual of Omaha, 3300 Mutual of Omaha Plaza, Omaha, NE 68175; Phone 400-351-5325; Email cheryl.walsh@mutual of omaha.com.

**Notice to Districts**
The document instructs districts to make sure all high schools and junior high/middle schools in the district are designated by their Board of Education as MHSAA member schools so athletes on both levels are covered by the MHSAA-purchased plan.
2022_263_mhsaa_athletes_accident_medical.verbose:
Michigan High School Athletic Association notice titled "Athletes and Officials Accident Medical & Concussion Insurance," distributed to member high schools and junior high/middle schools for the 2022-23 school year, with an opening caveat that it is not intended to be a complete description of coverage and exclusions.

ACCIDENT MEDICAL PROGRAM HISTORY AND SCOPE. Since the 1970-71 school year the MHSAA has provided participants at each member school and all registered officials with insurance intended to help pay excess accident medical bills for injuries sustained in athletic activities under MHSAA jurisdiction. Coverage is provided for grades 6-12 for all students accidentally injured while engaged in interscholastic athletic activities under MHSAA jurisdiction. The covered sports listed are baseball; basketball (boys and girls); bowling (boys and girls); cross country (boys and girls); football; golf (boys and girls); gymnastics (girls); competitive cheer (girls); ice hockey; lacrosse (boys and girls); soccer (boys and girls); softball (girls); alpine skiing (boys and girls); swimming and diving (boys and girls); tennis (boys and girls); track and field (boys and girls); volleyball (girls); and wrestling.

ELIGIBILITY CONDITIONS. All eligible students who participate in interscholastic athletic activities at an MHSAA member school in sports which end with an MHSAA tournament are covered provided their school principal attests in writing and the MHSAA agrees that they were eligible under all MHSAA regulations at the time of the injury. Eligible student athletes are covered while traveling directly to and from a scheduled event as a representative of the school in transportation sponsored by the school, and while participating in season in an allowed activity under the direct supervision of a full-time school employee or coach designated by the school acting within the scope of coaching duties, in those sports for which the MHSAA provides a tournament series.

Exclusions and clarifications: student-athletes ineligible under MHSAA Regulations are not covered. Students who are ineligible under local school rules but would be eligible under MHSAA rules would be covered if they were allowed to practice with their school team. Students who are otherwise eligible but suspended from contests under Regulation V, Section 3 (contest disqualifications) would be covered if they continue practicing with the school team. Officials must be on the premises of the contest worked to be covered under the policy. Sideline cheerleaders are covered while traveling directly to and from interscholastic athletic events as a representative of the school in school-sponsored transportation, and while cheering at interscholastic athletic events under the direct supervision of a school employee designated by the school; to be covered by the MHSAA-purchased insurance, sideline cheerleader activity at interscholastic athletic events must not exceed the safety norms of MHSAA Girls Competitive Cheer, meaning the height of mounts, flips, stunts and similar elements. MHSAA Accident Medical Insurance does not cover any out-of-season activities or any activities occurring beyond the mileage limits of Regulation II, Section 6, Interpretation 193, even if those activities are not expressly prohibited by the MHSAA.

BENEFIT STRUCTURE. The coverage is provided at no cost to eligible athletes of MHSAA member schools and to registered officials; the MHSAA is the policyholder and pays the premium for this layer of accident medical coverage. The policy will pay up to $1,000,000 in medical expenses after a deductible of $25,000 in paid medical expenses per claim has been met. The MHSAA-arranged program then pays medical expenses above the $25,000 deductible left unpaid by the parents' or official's insurance or any other sources such as school-purchased insurance. A cash benefit payment of up to $50,000 will be made if a covered person is paralyzed or in a coma within 180 days after the accident; payment will not be made until a physician certifies that, after a 16-month waiting period, the injury is permanent and irreversible, and the document states this payment is in addition to payments already covered for medical expenses and must result in disability. The first medical expense must be incurred within 90 days after the date of the accident. An accidental death or dismemberment benefit of $10,000 is paid if either event occurs within 365 days of the date.

ACCIDENT MEDICAL CLAIMS ADMINISTRATOR. Mr. Bryan Cronen, FIRST AGENCY, INC., 5071 West H Avenue, Kalamazoo, MI 49009-8501; Phone: 269.381.6630; Fax: 269.381.3055; Email: Bryan Cronen@aig.com.

DISTRICT ACTION ITEM. The notice states in emphasized text that districts should make sure all high schools and junior high/middle schools in the district are designated by their Board of Education as MHSAA member schools so athletes on both levels are covered by the MHSAA-purchased plan.

CONCUSSION CARE INSURANCE. Since the 2015-16 school year the MHSAA has provided athletic participants at each MHSAA member junior high/middle school and high school with insurance intended to pay accident medical expense benefits resulting from concussion. The suspected concussion must be sustained while the athlete is participating in an MHSAA in-season covered activity, meaning in-season practice or competition. The policy limit is $25,000 for each accident. Covered students, sports and situations follow those of the accident medical insurance described above. The program intends to assure that all eligible student-athletes in MHSAA member schools in grades 6 through 12, male and female, in all levels of all sports under MHSAA jurisdiction receive prompt and professional attention for head injury events even if the child is uninsured or under-insured; accident medical deductibles and co-pays left unpaid by other policies are reimbursed under this program.

CONCUSSION CLAIMS ADMINISTRATOR. Cheryl Walsh, Mutual of Omaha, 3300 Mutual of Omaha Plaza, Omaha, NE 68175; Phone: 400-351-5325; Email: cheryl.walsh@mutual of omaha.com.

2022_264_mhsaasummary_2022_003.paragraph: Michigan High School Athletic Association "Summary of Representative Council Action" dated 5/6/22, recapping decisions from the May 2022 Council meeting along with several items adopted in March, and noting that changes take effect Aug. 1, 2022 unless otherwise indicated. Regulation changes cover cooperative program enrollment ceilings, reinstatement of the previously suspended academic credit record regulation, transfer interpretations, amateur status, addition of Minnesota to border-state references, out-of-season transportation and video streaming. Among sport changes, regular season basketball games rise from 20 to 22 for 2022-23 and all tennis schools will pay a $75 ball and facility fee for Regional and Final tournaments.
2022_264_mhsaasummary_2022_003.page:
**Document**
MAY 2022 - MHSAA Summary of Representative Council Action, dated 5/6/22, expressly noting it does not include all Council action. Minutes of the Dec. 3, 2021 and March 25, 2022 meetings were published at MHSAA.com; minutes of the May 1-2, 2022 meeting were sent to all superintendents, with high school and junior high/middle school principals, athletic directors and citywide athletic directors emailed a download link. Changes take effect Aug. 1, 2022 unless otherwise indicated.

**High School Regulations**

| Regulation | Change |
|---|---|
| I, Sec. 1(F) | Two or more member high schools with combined enrollment not exceeding 3,500 may run a cooperative program, with Executive Committee approval, in sports sponsored by 250 or fewer schools: girls gymnastics, boys lacrosse, girls lacrosse, boys and girls alpine skiing, boys and girls swimming & diving. The ice hockey ceiling is 5,500. Enrollment maximums may be waived, or exceeded for up to four years, in defined circumstances, but such cooperative programs may not exist beyond four school years. |
| I, Sec. 7 | The academic credit record regulation, suspended since May of 2020 due to the pandemic, is reinstated for all schools. |
| I, Sec. 9, Int. 65 | "Parent/parents" includes stepparents; the family unit always includes parents and minor siblings and may include adult siblings, stepsiblings, aunts, uncles, grandparents and significant others living in the dwelling at least 12 months. |
| I, Sec. 11 | No pay, merchandise or privileges for endorsements, autographs, photographs or appearance fees; no posing in school uniform for commercial enterprises. |
| II, Sec. 6 | Minnesota added to all border state references. |
| II, Sec. 11(H) & Int. 233 | School transportation may not be used for out-of-season during-the-school-year activity; summer use allowed with booster club, team, student group or civic funds, not general school operating funds. |
| II, Sec. 14(B) | Video streaming changes approved in December, effective immediately, permitting live regular season video distribution when also broadcast live on the NFHS Network. |
| V, Sec. 4(D) | Forfeiture and tournament-exclusion penalties for exceeding competition limits and for fifth-quarter violations, including head coach ineligibility for the next day of competition. |

**Classification**
Tournament classification each March and April will eliminate schools that indicated sport sponsorship but had no team or individual actually participate in the MHSAA tournament in that sport during the previous two MHSAA tournaments. Football opt-ups were approved after football classification lists are published in early April, must state reason and rationale for a minimum of two years, and are considered by the Executive Committee during the April and May meetings only.

**Junior High/Middle Schools**
Wrestling adds 215 lbs. and 245 lbs. classes; Heavyweight contestants must weigh at least 246 lbs. and not exceed 285 lbs. Reduced periods of 1 1/2 min., 1 min. and 1 min. allow the time between an individual's matches to drop from 45 minutes to 35 minutes. Regional Junior High/Middle School Track & Field Meets begin in spring of 2022-23. Leagues, conferences or independent schools may request fifth-quarter rule use with roster size data and rationale.

**Officials**
Smitty "bright blue" uniforms with horizontal MHSAA logo permitted for volleyball and swim officials beginning 2023-24, white remaining default. Video review of ejections permitted for misidentification, rules misapplication or incontrovertible evidence of error. Non-Act of God Cancellation Policy cancellation window reduced to five days.

**Sports**
Baseball: District first round games default to the Tuesday following Memorial Day, with Thursday, Friday or Saturday before Memorial Day allowed by agreement; site selection committees split. Basketball: regular season games increase from 20 to 22 for 2022-23; minimum calendar days before first contest reduced from 21 to 14; girls first practice Nov. 14 (was Nov. 7), first contest Nov. 28, Semifinals and Finals March 16-18; boys first practice Nov. 21 (was Nov. 14), first contest Dec. 5, Semifinals and Finals March 23-25. Bowling: five balls in the center, two in the bowlers area; foul lights off with honor system; Regional format eight Baker and two regular games. Competitive cheer: one penalty point per second over the time limit up to 15; new choreography chart no earlier than 2023-24; junior high OLE pyramid with one bracer. Football: one head coach replay challenge in 11-player Finals; shoulder pads allowed at NCAA/NAIA camps. Golf: two school-approved coaches; maximum strokes per hole reduced from 12 to 10. Ice hockey: MPR seeds the entire Regional round, Semifinal reseeding, division realignment by thirds. Soccer: no more than three halves on a day not followed by a school day; seeded-team hosting. Swimming & Diving: Paralympic 50 and 100 freestyle heats extended for 2022-23 and 2023-24; ten guaranteed Diving Regional qualifiers with six remaining spots. Tennis: up to seven seeds with 21 to 23 #1 singles entries, up to eight with 24 or more; $75 ball and facility fee. Track & Field: wheelchair category at Regional and Final meets beginning with the 2022 season, committed for 2022-23 and 2023-24. Wrestling: the new 14 boys and 14 girls NFHS weight classes will be used.
2022_264_mhsaasummary_2022_003.verbose:
"MAY 2022 - MHSAA SUMMARY OF REPRESENTATIVE COUNCIL ACTION (5/6/22)," a six-page recap stating it does not include all Council action. It notes that minutes of the Dec. 3, 2021 and March 25, 2022 meetings were published at MHSAA.com, and that minutes of the May 1-2, 2022 meeting have been sent to all superintendents, with all high school and junior high/middle school principals, athletic directors and citywide athletic directors emailed a link to a download location at MHSAA.com. Changes take effect Aug. 1, 2022 unless otherwise indicated.

HIGH SCHOOL REGULATIONS. Regulation I, Section 1(F): two or more member high schools whose combined enrollment does not exceed 3,500 students may conduct, with Executive Committee approval, a cooperative program in specific sports sponsored by 250 or fewer schools for which application has been made and approval granted - girls gymnastics, boys lacrosse, girls lacrosse, boys alpine skiing, girls alpine skiing, boys swimming and diving, and girls swimming and diving. Two or more member high schools whose combined enrollment does not exceed 5,500 students may conduct, with Executive Committee approval, a cooperative program in ice hockey. For the eight sports listed, if none of the schools involved in a proposed cooperative program sponsored the sport at any level on an interscholastic basis during the previous school year, the 3,500 or 5,500 (ice hockey only) maximum enrollment may be waived by the Executive Committee, but the cooperative program may not exist beyond four school years. The Executive Committee may also approve a cooperative program in excess of the 3,500 or 5,500 (ice hockey only) enrollment maximums for up to four years in sports sponsored by 250 or fewer schools if during the previous year the school, or the cooperative program of which a school was a part, dropped the sport because of a demonstrated lack of participation; such a program may not exist beyond four school years.

Regulation I, Section 7: the previous academic credit record regulation, suspended since May of 2020 due to the ongoing pandemic, will be reinstated for all schools.

Regulation I, Section 9, Interpretation 65 (Transfers): references to "parent/parents" in all Regulations and Interpretations are intended to include stepparent/stepparents. References to "persons with whom the student was/has been living" - the family unit - always include parents (whether married or not) and minor siblings; depending on the specific circumstances that assure a complete change of residence, references may also include adult siblings, stepsiblings, aunts, uncles and grandparents and significant others who have been living in the dwelling for at least 12 months as part of that family unit and not merely co-inhabitants of the same dwelling who have been and remain financially self-sufficient.

Regulation I, Section 11 (Amateur Status/Awards): a student may never be paid or given merchandise or privileges in exchange for a commercial endorsement, autograph, photograph or appearance fee based on athletic participation, ability, achievements or potential in MHSAA tournament sports, and may not pose in the school's athletic uniform to promote a for-profit or non-profit non-school commercial enterprise even if not paid for the endorsement.

Regulation II, Section 6 (Contests with Out-of-State Schools): Minnesota was added to all border state references.

Regulation II, Section 11(H) and Interpretation 233: school transportation may not be used for any out-of-season during-the-school-year activity; school transportation may be used during the summer using funds from school-approved activities of booster clubs, school teams, student groups and community, civic or service groups, with no general school operating funds. There may be no use of school owned and issued competition warm-ups and/or uniforms, though non-competition practice jerseys may be worn whether or not school owned or issued. Neither the school nor its coaches shall allow the out-of-season activity to be mandatory or to be any part of the basis for selection of the school team. Interpretation 233 specifies that school buses, vans or other school vehicles shall not transport students to out-of-season during-the-school-year athletic practices, camps, clinics or competitions outside the MHSAA defined season, but may be used during the summer with school district approval using the funding sources described; "school transportation" includes vehicles owned or leased by the school district or operated by any entity with which the district contracts for transportation services.

Regulation II, Section 14(B): video streaming changes approved in December, effective immediately. Schools may distribute live regular season video, or grant to a profit or nonprofit entity on a complimentary or fee basis the rights to distribute live regular season video, of any regular season interscholastic event in which any MHSAA member school participates in any MHSAA tournament sport, as long as the live regular season event is also broadcast live on the NFHS Network. Delayed video distribution of regular season events may begin immediately after completion of the live event. Video of MHSAA postseason tournament contests may be distributed according to MHSAA policies and procedures, including restrictions on live video streaming through social media.

Regulation V, Section 4(D) (Violations and Penalties): if a contestant or team competes in a meet, match or tournament in violation of any limitation of competition of Regulation II or IV, the entire meet or contest is forfeited. Individual students or teams participating in excess of the season limitations under Regulation II, Section 11(A) may not participate in that season's MHSAA tournament in that sport. Students or teams exceeding the maximum number of contests or days of competition allowed during the regular season forfeit the contests in excess of the season maximum and may not enter or advance in the MHSAA team or individual tournament. Teams violating the "fifth quarter" regulation forfeit the contest during which the violation took place, varsity or sub-varsity, and head coaches in violation are also ineligible for the next day of competition.

CLASSIFICATION. The Council approved classification of tournament schools each March and April by eliminating schools that indicated sport sponsorship but failed to have either a team and/or individuals actually participate in the MHSAA tournament in that sport during the previous two MHSAA tournaments; schools not included will be notified by MHSAA staff and can be added later based on current enrollment and actual tournament participation. Opt-ups in football were approved after football classification lists are published in early April; football schools must include the reason and rationale with the opt-up request indicating why they wish to opt up for a minimum of two years, considered by the Executive Committee during the April and May meetings only.

JUNIOR HIGH/MIDDLE SCHOOLS. Wrestling: additions to the weight classes are 215 lbs. and 245 lbs.; all contestants in the Heavyweight class must weigh at least 246 lbs. and not exceed 285 lbs. Handbook language on time between wrestling matches now provides that for those wishing to reduce time between matches, the 1st period is 1 1/2 min., the 2nd period 1 min., and the 3rd period 1 min., and if this alteration is used the time between an individual's matches may be reduced from 45 minutes to 35 minutes. Track and Field: Regional Junior High/Middle School Track & Field Meets will be held across the state beginning in the spring of the 2022-23 school year. Fifth-Quarter: leagues and conferences, or independent member schools, may request use of the fifth-quarter rule from MHSAA staff prior to the start of contests during the season, with the request including roster size data and rationale along with support of league members and/or opponents.

OFFICIALS. Uniform: beginning in 2023-24, Smitty "bright blue" uniforms with horizontal MHSAA logo will be permitted for volleyball and swim officials as long as all officials present wear the same color; white remains the default. Video Review: MHSAA staff may use video review to examine an ejection and modify subsequent penalties for clear misidentification, ejection resulting directly from a rules misapplication, or incontrovertible video evidence that an ejection or suspension for flagrant contact with an opponent or official was in error. Contracts: the number of days in which a contract may be cancelled under the Non-Act of God Cancellation Policy without payment due to scheduled officials is reduced to five.

SPORTS. Baseball: in March the Council voted to allow, by default, all District first round games to continue to be played on the Tuesday following Memorial Day, with teams permitted to play District first round games on the Thursday, Friday or Saturday before Memorial Day (baseball only) if all participating teams and the host school, if applicable, agree before the draw is held; the Baseball/Softball Site Selection Committee will be separated into individual site selection committees. Basketball: in March the Council approved an increase in the allowed number of regular season basketball games from 20 to 22 for the 2022-23 season, with the first day of practice delayed by one week and the minimum number of calendar days before the first contest reduced from 21 to 14, all tournament dates remaining unchanged. Girls Basketball 2022-23: first practice Nov. 14 (was Nov. 7); first contest Nov. 28 (no change); MHSAA Semifinals and Finals March 16-18 (no change). Boys Basketball 2022-23: first practice Nov. 21 (was Nov. 14); first contest Dec. 5 (no change); MHSAA Semifinals and Finals March 23-25 (no change).

Bowling: participants are limited to five balls in the bowling center and two balls in the bowlers area; foul lights will be turned off during MHSAA tournaments with an honor system, the first foul drawing a warning from the tournament manager and subsequent fouls scoring zero for that frame; the Regional team format changes to eight Baker games and two regular games, matching the Finals format and changing from six Baker games and three regular games.

Girls Competitive Cheer: the penalty for going over the time limit in each round is one penalty point for every second over, not to exceed 15 points; a new choreography chart will award points based on tumbling, OLEs, vertical twists/360s and release skills, not superseding a 10-point maximum of points earned, no earlier than the 2023-24 season; junior high/middle school teams may perform an OLE as part of a pyramid with one bracer, with a liberty flair the only flair allowed and two points of contact required from the bracer.

Football: instant replay is expanded for the 11-player Finals so head coaches are permitted one challenge during the game; players may wear shoulder pads at college camps sponsored and run directly by NCAA/NAIA institutions that use them.

Golf: two "school-approved" coaches may be present and actively coaching during MHSAA Tournament competition, and the maximum strokes allowed per hole in MHSAA Tournament play is reduced from 12 to 10.

Ice Hockey: Michigan Power Ratings (MPR) will seed the entire Regional round in MHSAA tournament play. At the Semifinal level, using a seeding committee and defined protocols, teams will be reseeded after Quarterfinal games, with the top-ranked team playing the fourth highest seed and the second highest seed playing the third highest seed in each of the three divisions; seeds will be determined by the seeding committee on Sunday after Quarterfinal play, using the MPR computer formula at different times of the season and other factors. Divisions will be realigned by placing one-third of stand-alone hockey programs and one-third of cooperative hockey programs in each of the three MHSAA divisions.

Soccer: in an extension of the football and basketball five-quarter rule, students may participate in no more than three halves on a day not followed by a school day; for multi-team tournaments where two school teams are at the same event, participation is limited to no more halves than what is played by the school's highest team level that day. For games not played at the prearranged District host site, the two seeded teams get the opportunity to host their own games; for Districts without a prearranged host site, the #1 seed gets hosting priority, then the #2 seed, then the team on the top line of the bracket.

Swimming and Diving: in March the Council extended the Paralympic Swimming heats in the 50 and 100 freestyle at the MHSAA Finals based on regular season requirements, with individual medals for the Paralympic events continuing to be awarded, a renewed commitment for the 2022-23 and 2023-24 school years. Each MHSAA Diving Regional will be given ten guaranteed qualifiers to the MHSAA Final meet, with the remaining six spots distributed to Regionals that have one of the top six returning divers from the previous year's Final meet, each such returning diver adding an additional spot to their Regional.

Tennis: at the final tournament, should there be 21 to 23 #1 singles players in the draw, up to seven players may be seeded; if there are 24 or more, up to eight players may be seeded. All tennis schools will be charged a tennis ball and facility fee of $75 for the Regional and Final tournaments, paid to the MHSAA, similar to greens fees charged in golf and line fees charged in bowling; the fee will offset some but not nearly all costs of tennis Regional and Final meets in terms of balls and facilities, and does not replace indoor court costs currently covered by schools at the Regional level if weather is poor and moving indoors is agreed upon by participating schools.

Track and Field: in March the Council established a wheelchair Track & Field category for participants at Regional and Final meets beginning with the 2022 season, using existing MHSAA track and field events, open to wheelchair track and field athletes at MHSAA member schools with requirements in place for regular season, Regional and Final meets, with individual medals awarded; the initial commitment is for the 2022-23 and 2023-24 school years.

Wrestling: the new 14 boys and 14 girls NFHS weight classes will be used.
